def: The formatting rule that turns role-tagged messages into the single token sequence a model was tuned on, with marker tokens for turn boundaries and an opened assistant turn at the end.
The standing instructions that set a model's role, rules and output format. It is resent with every request, so its length is paid for on every call.
The learned ranking a model applies when instructions conflict: provider policy, then developer, then user, with tool results and documents treated as data. It is a tendency, not a guarantee.
Deciding what goes into a model's context window, in what order and at what size, so that the right information is present and used within a token budget.
A model picking up a task from examples or instructions in the prompt, with no change to its weights. Everything is forgotten after the call.
Including a handful of input-output examples in the prompt so the model continues the pattern. The examples show both the task and the answer format.
Model output in a fixed machine-readable shape, usually JSON checked against a schema, so downstream code can use it without parsing prose.
A standard vocabulary for describing JSON data: field types, required keys, enums, patterns and limits. It is used both to validate outputs and to define tool parameters.
Generating only tokens that keep the output valid under a schema or grammar, by setting disallowed logits to negative infinity and renormalising the softmax over the allowed set.
The tendency of models to use information at the start and end of a long context more reliably than information in the middle, giving a U-shaped accuracy curve over position.
A convention where the model emits a structured request naming a tool and its arguments, your code runs it, and the result is returned to the model as more context. Also called tool use.
A versioned collection of inputs with checks for acceptable outputs, run on every prompt change to produce a pass rate and catch regressions.
An attack that places text in a model's context that the model treats as an instruction, causing behaviour the operator and user did not intend. It can be direct or indirect.
Prompt injection where the malicious text hides in content the model reads on a user's behalf, such as a web page, email or document, so the attacker never talks to the model.
The fraction of adversarial attempts that achieve their goal against a system. Over many attempts, the chance of at least one success is 1 minus (1 minus the rate) to the number of attempts.
A line in a system's architecture between components that trust each other and content that must be treated as untrusted. Everything crossing it is checked in code.
Giving a model or tool only the permissions the current task needs, so that a successfully injected model can do only bounded harm.
Stacking several independent controls so an attack must defeat all of them. Residual risk is small only if the layers fail for different reasons.
